title: Third-party scorer checks must run before import and before instantiation
answers: order of validation when restoring a third-party scorer
why is a non-Scorer class rejected before construction
where should new checks for third-party scorer payloads go
body:
Invariant: in Scorer.model_validate, all payload checks (allow-list, required fields, metric_name identifier, kwargs metric_name) run before importlib.import_module. After import, the resolved attribute must be a class and a Scorer subclass before it is instantiated.
Enforced by: mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py:Scorer.model_validate (the `inspect.isclass(scorer_class) and issubclass(scorer_class, Scorer)` check precedes construction).
What breaks if skipped: an import with side effects runs on a bad payload, or a non-Scorer attribute's constructor runs as defense-in-depth is lost.
Constraints: new validation for third-party payloads belongs before the import_module call; tests should patch mlflow.genai.scorers.base.importlib.import_module and assert it is not called on rejected payloads, as tests/genai/scorers/test_serialization.py does.
applies: Any new check added to third-party scorer deserialization in mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py.
says: Reject malformed third-party evaluation metric configurations before loading external modules.
Restoring an invalid custom scorer runs untrusted module code during import.
Ensure third-party evaluators validate required fields before importing dependencies.
Prevent non-scorer classes from being constructed when restoring evaluation metrics.
Loading a damaged custom evaluation metric triggers unexpected module side effects.
search: Third-party scorer deserialization in Scorer.model_validate must run all payload validation checks before calling importlib.import_module, and must verify the imported attribute is a Scorer subclass before instantiation. Performing validation prior to import prevents executing imports with side effects or running constructors of non-Scorer classes. Applies to new checks added in mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py, where tests should assert importlib.import_module is never called on rejected payloads.
